page: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g is a general-purpose virtual instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It is equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.0 GHz, supporting two threads per core. The configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB allocated per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions consist of 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Vector extensions and cryptographic instruction sets such as AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI are enabled. The server does not include GPU acceleration and provisions 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core execution speed contrasted with moderate multi-core throughput. Single-threaded evaluations show competitive figures, highlighted by top-tier results in stress-ng single-core tests, strong Geekbench single-core marks of 2009.0, and elevated compression rates in single-threaded gzip and bzip3. However, multi-core scaling is bounded by the underlying two-core physical topology, leading to lower-quartile performance in Geekbench multi-core scoring and multi-threaded compilation tasks. Uncached memory read bandwidth averages 69.83 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth reaches 41.08 GB/sec, supporting standard memory throughput across steady-state workloads.

With its dedicated core model and balanced memory profile, the vx1-g-4c-16g delivers qualitative cost efficiency for resource-steady workloads that prioritize consistent CPU access without high multi-threaded concurrency. The 1 GB local NVMe footprint indicates that persistent state requires external network storage or centralized databases. As a result, this system is well configured for web application middleware, API gateways, Redis caching layers, and decoupled background worker tasks.
description: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz. The system provides 16.0 GB of memory, 32 MB of L3 cache, 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and no GPU hardware. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate high single-threaded compute efficiency, registering strong single-core scores in Geekbench and top-tier single-threaded compression throughput with AVX-512 support. Multi-core performance scales modestly due to the physical two-core constraint, resulting in lower scores on parallel software compilation. Memory bandwidth reaches 69.83 GB/sec on uncached reads, enabling stable performance in Redis operations and web throughput. Because local storage is limited to 1 GB, the instance is cost-effective primarily for stateless or network-attached architectures, such as microservices, web hosting, caching instances, and single-threaded batch processors.
